required_hypotheses: The ordered computational basis is fixed; the exact displayed X, Y, Z matrices and the sign of Y must be used.
incoming_direct.actual_supplier_excerpt:
In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

required_hypotheses: H=(X+Z)/sqrt(2), T=diag(1,e^{i pi/4}), and their exact scalar phases are retained.
incoming_direct.actual_supplier_excerpt:
In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

required_hypotheses: For real theta, P_theta=diag(1,e^{i theta}) and the control-first CP(theta)=diag(1,1,1,e^{i theta}) convention.
incoming_direct.actual_supplier_excerpt:
For a real angle $\theta$, define the one-qubit phase matrix $P_\theta=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\theta})$. In control-first order define

$$CP(\theta):=C(P_\theta)=\operatorname{diag}(1,1,1,e^{i\theta})$$

in the ordered basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$. This is the exact controlled phase; no circuit cost or controlled access to an arbitrary black-box unitary is implied.

required_hypotheses: For unit scalar lambda and a target unitary U, C(lambda U)=(P_lambda tensor I)C(U), in control-first order.
incoming_direct.actual_supplier_excerpt:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional target space, let $U$ be unitary on $H$, and let $|\lambda|=1$. In control-first order put
$$C(U)=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}.$$
Then $C(\lambda U)=(P_\lambda\otimes I_H)C(U)$. A scalar multiplying an entire output leaves every defined finite-POVM outcome law unchanged, whereas a scalar attached to a target matrix inside a control gives a phase on only the active control block; applying $P_{\overline\lambda}$ on the control restores the exact controlled matrix.

page_prerequisite_gaps.actual_supplier_excerpt:
For $n\ge2$, every $n$-qubit unitary has an exact no-ancilla circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and at most
$$\frac{23}{48}4^n-\frac32 2^n+\frac43$$
CNOTs. For $n=0$ or $n=1$, no CNOT is needed. This is a gate-count bound; it makes no numerical decomposition-time or finite-precision bit-complexity claim.
